title: Run Code When a Tenant Starts | Orchard Core
description:
Some code has to run when a tenant starts: warming a cache, checking a folder, or writing a log entry. A module's Startup class registers services and middleware; to run your own code as a tenant starts, a module needs a tenant event handler.

Orchard Core calls the tenant event handlers that a module registers. You implement IModularTenantEvents, or inherit from ModularTenantEvents, register the class in your Startup class, and its methods run when the tenant activates, terminates, or is removed.

In this video:
• When a tenant starts: activation and tenant events
• Write a handler: the interface and its base class
• Register the handler in your Startup class
• The order of the events: registration order and its reverse
• Run it: when the handler is called
• Stopping and removing: TerminatingAsync, TerminatedAsync and RemovingAsync
• Write handlers with care: errors and the state of the tenant
